messages:
nina: Alerting thread - sudden p95/p99 increase for generation endpoints on dedicated-pool-2 starting ~06:30 UTC. p50 unchanged, but p95 ~2x and p99 ~4x. A few customer retries and some 504s. No app-level deploys. Opening for infra triage.

tom: Thanks. Which model + route and any slow request IDs? I'll start looking at node metrics and storage logs. I see NVMe latency spikes on telemetry around 06:28.

nina: Route /v1/generate (model: redwood-turbo-3b). Slow reqs: gen-cc102, gen-cc104. Window 06:28-06:45 UTC. App-side flamegraphs point to time spent waiting on fsync/poll and increased syscall wait.

kevin: Pulled iostat and dmesg from node dp2-15. iostat shows nvme %util ~98% and avg await high. dmesg contains repeated lines:

```
[06:31:12] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 0
[06:31:15] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x1a2f timed out, aborting
[06:31:17] nvme nvme0: controller reset due to I/O timeout
```

% iostat snippet:
```
Device:    r/s    w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1  110.7  58.4  10880  4600  16.5   7.3    0.62  98.7
```

arya: Noted. We did a rolling CUDA runtime + driver bump (CUDA 12.5 + NVIDIA 540.17) to a subset of pools overnight; dp2 had the update applied around 06:00 UTC. Also bumped kernel to 6.1.11 in the same image. Could be an interaction.

infra-bot: deploy: image-update applied to dedicated-pool-2 (subset) by arya at 06:00 UTC.

kevin: To get fast signal: i'm going to canary-rollback driver on dp2-15 to previous driver 535.xx and watch p99. If it improves, that'll be strong evidence. Also capturing blktrace and perf for reproduction.

canary-bot: canary-rollback initiated on dedicated-pool-2/dp2-15 by kevin at 06:42 UTC. Status: in progress.

nina: I'm steering traffic away from dp2-15 and increasing prefix cache TTL to reduce persistence writes. Also lowering worker batch concurrency from 16->6 as a short-term throttle.

kevin: After rollback on dp2-15 p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~420ms within ~2 minutes for traffic hitting that node. dmesg on that host no longer shows controller resets. Other nodes on dp2 still showing resets where new driver installed.

tom: Good signal. Next steps: 1) reproduce offline with fio + same kernel/driver combo and our IO pattern; 2) capture blktrace/perf and send to vendor/NVIDIA; 3) hold fleet rollout until we have vendor guidance. For mitigation, we can expand runtime throttle and keep traffic shifted.

kevin: I ran fio on an affected node with iodepth=64 bs=4k randwrite mix and triggered controller resets with the new driver/kernel - previous image did not. Attaching fio job and blktrace output to ticket.

vendor-bot: vendor ticket created with NVMe vendor & NVIDIA by kevin at 07:30 UTC. Logs uploaded: dmesg, blktrace, fio outputs, kernel perf. Reference: INC-2456789012.

arya: In the medium term we should implement adaptive NVMe submission pacing in the runtime: limit max in-flight nvme submissions per-worker and reactive backpressure when device latency rises. Also add a fio-based smoke test to the kernel/driver canary pipeline to catch these regressions earlier.

tom: Agreed. Short-term plan: 1) keep rollbacks on impacted nodes and pause further driver/kernel rollouts; 2) maintain runtime concurrency caps and extended cache TTL for the pool; 3) add node-agent guard to divert traffic if controller resets observed >3 within 5m; 4) vendor engagement and reproduce matrix (kernel vs driver vs firmware).

nina: I'll notify customers with a concise update (mitigation in place, vendor engaged, ETA 48-72h for vendor analysis). Filing postmortem and action items: kevin -> vendor coord + fio matrix, arya -> runtime pacing RFC, tom -> node-agent guard, nina -> customer comms/postmortem.

canary-bot: traffic-shift: 35% of generation traffic moved off dedicated-pool-2 by nina at 07:02 UTC.

vendor-bot: Vendor initial reply: "We can reproduce timeouts under high small-block concurrency with driver 540.x on certain controller microcode versions. Recommending either firmware microcode update or driver pacing workaround. We'll follow up with patched firmware candidate." — vendor-eng at 08:10 UTC.

kevin: While waiting for vendor, i'll script an automated fio smoke test that mimics our KV persister: lots of small random fsyncs and high iodepth bursts. We'll add to the canary pipeline asap.

arya: I'll draft the RFC for adaptive pacing and include a safe rollout plan: start with per-worker soft caps, metric-driven backpressure, and emergency throttle hook for controller-reset detection.

tom: Thanks all. For now incident status: mitigated — customer-visible impact reduced with rollbacks and throttles, but root cause pending vendor fix. We'll reconvene on vendor patch tests. :white_check_mark:
